structure: Part 3, commodity type and the set-owned commodity vocabulary. Read in full: every file of src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/journeys/linear/features/commodity-type/ (page.js, controller.js, evaluation.js, template.njk, controller.test.js, commodity-type.fit.spec.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js, copy/copy.test.js) and both files of src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/services/commodities/ (index.js, commodities.test.js). Read for context, claimed by other parts: journeys/linear/flow/flow.js (part 2), src/server/app/shared/kit.js (part 13), and - to say where each branch of the answer leads, which this part's covers demands - shared/paths.js, shared/copy.en.js saveActions, journeys/linear/flow/entry-guard.js, journeys/linear/features/timing-windows.js, journeys/linear/features/commodities/links.js and fields.js key names, journeys/linear/features/hub/copy/copy.en.js row title, journeys/linear/flow/section-captions/copy/copy.en.js, journeys/linear/test-support.js helpers and fixtures, obligations/sections/commodity.js, obligations/sections/arrival.js and obligations/sections/parties.js. Covered: the one page of this slice, commodity-type, at /high-risk-plants/notifications/{journeyId}/commodity-type - its route, its place as the journey's entry page and guard, its caption, heading, hint and warning, its three radio options with label and timing hint, its required-answer rule and the one error message, its three save controls and Back behaviour in five trail states, what it commits, the line reconciliation a change of type triggers, its save-failure and stale-token answers, every copy key of copy.en.js and copy.cy.js verbatim, the 17 tests of commodity-type.fit.spec.js and the 32 of controller.test.js and copy/copy.test.js, the whole vocabulary services/commodities/index.js serves (3 commodity types, 9 categories, 15 genera, 3 origin constraints, 9 per-line fields and every narrowing between them) with its prototype-independent owner question recorded, evaluation.js as a mechanism, and every branch the commodity-type answer opens in the obligation model, the potato branch that skips arrival status included. Stops at the commodities list and details pages, which part 4 claims.

claims.statement: The service offers three commodity types, in this order: potatoes, plants for planting, wood and cut trees.
claims.quote:
const COMMODITY_TYPES = Object.freeze([
  'potatoes',
  'plants-for-planting',
  'wood-and-cut-trees'
])
claims.note: Which commodity types a notification may be for, and in what order they are offered, is not the prototype's to decide: it is a question for V4 (what the notification captures) or MDM through reference-data (if commodity types become a reference list). This claim records what the set hard-codes today, not a requirement.

claims.statement: The service offers nine categories of goods, in this order: seed potatoes, ware potatoes, plants for planting, trees for planting, conifer wood with bark, conifer wood without bark, cut coniferous trees, hardwood round surface, hardwood chips.
claims.quote:
const CATEGORIES = Object.freeze([
  SEED_POTATOES,

  PLANTS_FOR_PLANTING,

  CONIFER_WOOD_WITH_BARK,
  CONIFER_WOOD_WITHOUT_BARK,
  CUT_CONIFEROUS_TREES,
  HARDWOOD_ROUND_SURFACE,
  HARDWOOD_CHIPS
])
claims.note: The set calls these the nine statutory categories. Which categories the notification offers is V4's or MDM's to own, not the prototype's; this records the hard-coded list only.

claims.statement: The service knows fifteen genus entries: Castanea, Cedrus, Coffea, Fraxinus, Lavandula, Nerium oleander, Olea europaea, Picea, Pinus, Platanus, Polygala myrtifolia, Prunus, Quercus, Salvia rosmarinus, Ulmus. Four of them are species rather than genera, because the regulation lists them that way.
claims.quote:
// The fifteen entries of reg 26(1)(a). Four are species rather than genera;
// the regulation lists them that way and so does this list.
const GENERA = Object.freeze([
  CASTANEA,
  'Cedrus',
  'Coffea',
  FRAXINUS,
  'Lavandula',
  'Nerium oleander',
  'Olea europaea',
  'Picea',
  'Pinus',
  PLATANUS,
  'Polygala myrtifolia',
  'Prunus',
  'Quercus',
  'Salvia rosmarinus',
  'Ulmus'
])
claims.note: Whether the notification asks for a genus at all, and from what list, is V4's or MDM's to own. This records the set's hard-coded list and the regulation it cites.

claims.statement: A plants-for-planting or trees-for-planting line may name any of the fifteen genus entries.
A hardwood round-surface or hardwood-chips line may name only Castanea, Fraxinus or Platanus, so the page never offers fifteen entries and then rejects twelve.
A line of any other category - seed potatoes, ware potatoes, conifer wood with bark, conifer wood without bark or cut coniferous trees - is offered no genus at all.
claims.quote:
expect(generaFor(SEED_POTATOES)).toEqual([])
    expect(generaFor(CONIFER_WOOD_WITH_BARK)).toEqual([])

claims.statement: Exactly the categories that are offered a genus are the ones the genus field applies to, so no line is asked for a genus it has no list for.
A ware-potato line may originate only from Poland, Portugal, Romania or Spain.
claims.note: Which countries a reference list offers is MDM's through reference-data; which categories a rule covers is V4's. This records the set's own hard-coded narrowing.

claims.statement: A conifer-wood-without-bark line may originate only from Italy, France, Portugal or Spain.

A plants-for-planting, trees-for-planting, conifer-wood-with-bark, cut-coniferous-trees, hardwood-round-surface or hardwood-chips line may originate only from one of the 27 member States of the European Union, which the set holds as the origin block minus Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland.
claims.note: The set records its own reason for holding this country list in code rather than taking it from reference-data; the owner question for the list is still MDM's.

claims.statement: A consignment that breaks more than one origin rule is told about the narrowest one, because the rules are held narrowest first and the origin page reports failures in that order.
claims.quote:
The order is the order the origin page reports a failure in: a consignment
 * that breaks more than one constraint is told about the narrowest.

claims.statement: A seed-potato line is narrowed by no origin rule, because the statute scopes it to the whole Common SPS Area, so every country the origin page offers stays acceptable for it.
claims.quote:
Each constraint names the categories it binds and the countries those
 * categories may come from. A category the list never names — seed potatoes,
 * scoped by reg 24A(1)(a) to the whole Common SPS Area — narrows nothing, so
 * every country the origin block offers stays acceptable for it.

claims.statement: The commodity vocabulary holds values only, never the words a page shows for them: every label and hint is a copy leaf in the feature that renders it.
claims.quote:
The service holds values, never the words a page shows for them: a label or
 * a hint is a copy leaf in the feature that renders it. Keeping the values
 * here is what stops a volatile list being retyped into an obligation or a
 * copy module, where nothing would hold the two in step.

claims.statement: Only a potato notification is asked for the expected time of arrival; every other commodity type is asked a date alone.

Reg 24A(2)(a) asks potatoes for 'the expected time and date of their

 * a potato matter and the engine purges it when a notification changes to

Reg 24A(2)(aa) is the only landing element in the statute; reg 26(2) has
 * none, so plants and wood are never asked.

claims.statement: Nothing in this slice names an owner outside the service for the commodity vocabulary: the commodity types, the nine categories, the fifteen genus entries, the per-line field list and the origin country lists are all hard-coded in the set, with no call to reference-data or any other source of master data.
claims.note: Looked in services/commodities/index.js, its test, the commodity-type controller's imports and the copy bundles. The file's own docstring explains why the values live there rather than in a copy module or an obligation, but names no upstream owner. The programme's goal puts every piece of data with V4 or with MDM through reference-data, so the owner of each list is an open question this extract cannot settle.

claims.statement: The hint tells a trader to notify potatoes, plants for planting and wood in separate notifications, but nothing in this slice lets them start the second notification from here, link the two, or tells them what to do with a consignment holding more than one type.
claims.note: Looked at the page's copy bundle, its template, its controller and its 17 fit tests. The instruction is copy only: the page offers one radio group and no onward route for a second notification.

claims.statement: Nothing in this slice says whether a trader may change the commodity type of a notification that has already been submitted or is being amended: the page shows the same form and accepts the same post whatever the notification's status.
claims.note: Looked for a read-only branch, an amend check or a status check in the controller, its template and its unit and fit tests, and found none; the only status-dependent element on the page is the shared journey strip's Cancel amend control, which shared/kit.js owns. Changing the type of a submitted notification would drop its commodity lines under claim repo-plantsfrontend-p3-056.
